title: Idiomatic Kotlin Patterns
subtopics: Replace Boilerplate with Appropriate Language Features
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of idiomatic kotlin patterns using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates idiomatic kotlin patterns.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Idiomatic Kotlin Patterns** as part of **Functional Programming and Idiomatic Kotlin**. Apply idiomatic kotlin patterns by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail. Use the subtopics—Prefer Expressions Where Clear, Use val by Default, Replace Boilerplate with Appropriate Language Features—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: These concepts help you model domain rules and reusable APIs. Good boundaries reduce accidental mutation, unsafe casts, and code that is difficult to extend.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Idiomatic Kotlin Patterns removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
